cards.title: Strong demand, expensive capital
cards.question: Can AI earnings overcome a higher discount rate?
cards.selfCheck: Check CPI, yields and earnings revisions.
cards.prompt: Compare Nov 10 CPI (+0.4% monthly, above +0.3% forecast), Treasury yields and AI earnings revisions. Explain why strong demand can coexist with falling multiples; reject a rates-led bear case if yields ease and breadth improves.

cards.title: A chip rebound needs breadth
cards.question: Is risk appetite expanding beyond a few AI names?
cards.prompt: Check SOXX vs QQQ, RSP vs SPY, IWM and credit spreads across 7/30 days. Confirm or reject breadth improvement; do not treat premarket gains as proof.

cards.title: Foundry sales validate demand
cards.question: What does TSMC growth prove—and not prove?
cards.selfCheck: Check TSMC sales vs customer margins.
cards.prompt: Use TSMC's Nov 10 October revenue release: NT$586.89B, +59.7% YoY; Jan–Oct +43.3%. Distinguish verified foundry demand from hypotheses about NVDA, AMD, MU and customer returns. Source: https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3349

cards.title: Backlog is not cash flow
cards.question: When will prior AI commitments turn profitable?
cards.selfCheck: Check backlog, utilization and free cash flow.
cards.prompt: Trace 2026 AI data-center commitments into 2027 commissioning, utilization and cash generation. Distinguish contracted backlog from realized revenue; look for delays, financing costs and order revisions.

cards.title: 2027 budgets face a rate test
cards.question: What could change the AI earnings path in 1–9 months?
cards.prompt: Map 2027 hyperscaler capex guidance and the December 2026 Fed decision. Bull: orders and utilization rise while yields stabilize. Bear: high financing costs, delays or reduced capex. Check dates against official releases.

cards.title: Suppliers must prove resilience
cards.question: Can chip suppliers outperform AI infrastructure builders?
cards.prompt: Test over 30–90 days: MU, optical/networking and semicap vs financing-heavy AI operators. Bull case requires earnings upgrades and stable credit; reject if orders weaken or supplier relative returns lag. Separate 7/30/90-day evidence from hypothesis.
